items.title: From Endpoint to Funhouse: Changes in Ransomware Families and Kimsuky-Related Distribution Cases
items.content: A North Korean threat actor distributed Funhouse ransomware through malicious Korean-language documents disguised as resumes. Funhouse is a variant of the previously observed Endpoint ransomware. The attack chain involves multi-stage scripts including Batch, VBS, and PowerShell, leading to Quasar RAT installation before deploying the final ransomware payload. items.title: Analysis of Wpcdoor Attack Case Distributed Through Domestic DVR Management Software
items.content: A South Korean company's DVR management software (CMS) was exploited to distribute the Wpcdoor backdoor malware. The attack chain begins when CMS.exe installs rs.win32.exe along with a malicious IPHLPAPI.DLL file that loads via DLL side-loading. This first-stage downloader retrieves WpcMon.exe and samcli.dll, which acts as a second-stage downloader executing the Wpcdoor backdoor in memory.... This pulse includes 15 indicators of compromise (IOCs). Associated malware: Wpcdoor, IPHLPAPI.DLL, QtCore4.dll.

items.title: A New ESXi Implant Linked to Settra Ransomware
